harbor_p10_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_001.text: The twelfth week began with the office moving Yue's loaned writing board onto the return shelf whenever her shift ended. Nothing dramatic had changed. The original appointment was simply reaching the date everyone wrote at the start. Han Pei called it closure, which sounded severe until she explained the tasks: check shifts, pay the final wages, reconcile expenses, inspect borrowed items and close lodging charges. Yue appreciated the ordinary list. It allowed her to finish a term without pretending the harbor had finished all the work that made the term useful.

harbor_p10_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_002.text: The first remaining shift went to the permit refund contact questions linked to the original households. Two payers were still owed two copper each. A destination keeper had located one through a lodging notice; the other had replied under a shortened hiring name requiring identity comparison. Yue could prepare the relevant source links under supervision. The permit clerk would decide the collection authority. Four copper seemed a small task until every name had to be right. The office refused to make smallness a reason for allowing the last recipients to receive less careful work.

harbor_p10_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_003.text: The located payer chose a scheduled collection route through the canal village office. The keeper verified his authorization and sent the two alongside an ordinary existing transfer. Its acknowledgment returned within the week. The other worker's current identity evidence matched the earlier charge through the full hiring reference and a witnessed account. He collected his two at the permit desk. Fifty-eight copper had now reached all twenty-nine identified payers. The refund account closed at zero under its own receipts. Zeng received the permitted completion notice, rather than an opportunity to reclaim someone else's uncollected share.

harbor_p10_004.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_004.text: He Ming read the final aggregate and put her own receipt away with a satisfaction she did not want to name too loudly. The two copper already bought thread and a small packet of tea. Both things were ordinary, which seemed the point. Dai Min said she spent her refund on a needle case and would refuse any public account claiming the harbor restored her happiness. He Ming laughed. The women could acknowledge a completed remedy without letting it become the whole story others told about their losses.

harbor_p10_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_005.text: The barge crew's grounding interval remained under its separate contract review. Undisputed wages had been paid, and current safe shore work continued under explicit terms. Shui Rong received a status reply identifying the competent office and next date. Yue copied the public completion limits into the initial-term report with private pages closed. There was no need to pretend the new question belonged to the old wage guarantee simply because it arrived before she departed. That deposit had closed correctly. The harbor still owed the crew a working referral and a clear current answer.

harbor_p10_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_006.text: Shui asked whether Yue's departure would make the question disappear. Han said the assigned adviser held responsibility beyond the visitor's term and showed the existing reference. Shui tested the route herself, asking the adviser to read back the next step. He did. The small check reassured her more than a promise that Yue would stay until every issue ended. He Ming watched and resisted offering herself as another permanent messenger. She could remain a friend to the crew without making their whole contract question a task only her feet knew how to carry.

harbor_p10_007.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_007.text: The term-review meeting used a plain table at the north office. The administrator invited staff with relevant duties, two claimant delegates chosen by specific consent, and Yue. Han supplied the shift and expense record. He Ming supplied examples of wrong walks and useful replies. Yan supplied work-line reporting experience. Sui supplied the separation between contact, cargo and technical questions. The people had learned to trust one another enough to disagree without making every disagreement proof of indifference. That trust did not create money. The administrator placed actual proposed allocations beside their requests.

harbor_p10_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_008.text: The initial appropriation was one hundred ninety-two copper. Twenty-four half-days at two earned forty-eight wages when completed. Bed and meals over the twelve-week term totaled the agreed seventy-two. Copies used ten, interpreters twelve, ferries six. The projected final actual spending was therefore one hundred forty-eight, leaving forty-four unspent within the operations appropriation. The last shifts and lodging invoice still needed completion before closure. Yue checked the arithmetic with her own pencil. She would receive no private bonus from unused expense ceilings, and no one proposed making the remainder disappear into a convenient new task.

harbor_p10_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_009.text: The administrator asked why continued work should receive a new allocation if forty-four remained from the old. Han explained that the old authority named a finite term and tasks. Unspent operations money remained operations money, but did not authorize an indefinite appointment. A new term needed its own approved purpose and total, whether the larger office drew on the same treasury or another eligible line. The administrator agreed and asked for a bounded proposal. Yue liked the distinction. It made continuation an actual decision rather than an old purse kept open because affection made the ending awkward.

harbor_p10_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_010.text: The proposed term ran fourteen weeks, from the thirteenth through the twenty-sixth harbor week. It offered twenty-eight half-days at two copper, fifty-six in wages. Bed and meals would be eighty-four at the negotiated rate. Ferries had a twenty-four ceiling; copies and interpreters eighteen each. The total was two hundred. Its source was a newly authorized ordinary harbor operations allocation, reserved before any contract began. Claimant refunds, merchant accounts and the closed guarantee supplied none. Yue read the terms without answering immediately. A genuine offer deserved more thought than the relief of being asked to stay.

harbor_p10_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_011.text: The job would test and document contact routes across office, outreach and work-line intake, with named ordinary staff continuing questions beyond Yue's scheduled shifts. She could carry permitted requests, compare relevant copies and report actual outcomes. Decisions on wages, permits, commercial title, care and technical safety remained with competent people. The terms did not buy unlimited qi or every free evening. Han insisted unsuccessful attempts be recorded as well as successes. He Ming insisted people refusing help retain ordinary access. Yan required work-line tasks to follow the responsible foreman's safety instructions. All three conditions went into the draft.

harbor_p10_012.speaker: harbor_sui_yan
harbor_p10_012.text: Before you agree, ask what you want from fourteen more weeks. The town has need enough to make anyone staying look generous. That is no reason to hide the choice from yourself. I would value the work. I would also manage tomorrow's cargo questions if you left. Han has an office, He Ming has people who ask her, and Yan has his lane. You are allowed to see a road beyond us without calling it abandonment. If you stay, let the agreement carry a job you want to do, rather than a sentence you are afraid to refuse.

harbor_p10_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_013.text: He Ming looked down at the draft. She wanted Yue to stay because she trusted her, not merely because another fourteen weeks would improve forms. Saying that aloud felt childish after so many arguments about authority. She said it anyway. The room went quiet until Han admitted she wanted the same. Yue felt the offer become harder and kinder at once. Friendship belonged in her decision, though it could not create contractual duty. She asked for a day to consider the terms and received it. The existing term would close on schedule either way.

harbor_p10_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_014.text: Yue went to the shore path with her travel book. A road inland crossed low hills before reaching towns with workshops she knew only through travelers' reports. She had no appointment there, which made departure feel both free and shapeless. Staying had names, hours and familiar stairs. She wondered whether she preferred it because it was safer. The question had no clerk. She walked beyond the last boat shed and let the harbor sounds fade enough to notice her own breathing. The sea offered neither encouragement nor a reason to become braver than she actually felt.

harbor_p10_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_015.text: At supper, the repair shed keeper asked whether Yue intended to take the new term. Yue said she was deciding. The woman supplied the new lodging rate already negotiated with the office and the private rate if Yue chose a short interval without employment. She could accept a guest without approving a life choice. Yue appreciated the plainness. The keeper's son asked whether leaving meant the fish kite lost its best legal adviser. Fen, washing a cup nearby, said its legal advisers were the reason it kept losing arguments. The boy found that answer offensive enough to cheer everyone.

harbor_p10_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_016.text: Han visited with her painted board, which now stood at home rather than the office. She had arranged another paid beginner session and wanted to show Yue a curve that finally obeyed the brush. The curve looked ordinary. Han's pride did not. Yue admired it without suggesting the clerk must become a painter immediately. Then they discussed the new schedule. Two half-days a week left room for Yue's personal practice and other choices. Han had her own roster and free sessions. Neither woman had to become the other's permanent remedy for a dissatisfied life.

harbor_p10_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_017.text: He Ming met Yue at the market the following morning carrying a list of food prices. She was considering a small shared packing arrangement with two neighbors if contracts could support it. Her present foreman paid reliably but assigned hours with little notice. The idea frightened her. She had argued that workers deserved choice and now discovered how much she wanted a clerk to certify her own risk harmless. Yue said they could compare actual terms with the labor adviser when ready. He Ming laughed and said she had come to discuss Yue's choice, then immediately tried to outsource hers.

harbor_p10_018.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_018.text: They bought cabbage, onions and a fish too small for He Ming's first recipe. She changed the meal rather than blame the seller after accepting its size. Yue noticed that practical flexibility looked easier in a kitchen than at a public counter. The woman said food forgave changes if people remained hungry enough. They ate with He Jun, who supplied a story about a boatman marrying a merchant's niece. The story's only evidence was his friend's confidence. Nobody believed it. They enjoyed it anyway, making an ordinary evening large enough for uncertain futures to rest inside it.

harbor_p10_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_019.text: Yue returned to the office and said she would take the fourteen-week term if the approved source, scope and schedule stayed as written. She wanted to see whether routes could work when she was absent, and to live among friends while learning that limit. The administrator confirmed the reserved two hundred and authorized the contract. Han entered its start after the initial term closed, with a fresh shift schedule. No salary was paid twice. The date did not promise Yue would stay forever. It gave her a real next beginning she could choose without turning the first ending into failure.

harbor_p10_020.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_020.text: The new agreement retained the separate qi-task condition: any cultivation use needed an agreed safe task under the responsible person, not a general demand from an employer. Yue remained fourth stage with two earned pairs. The administrator recorded no rank promotion, technical license or public office bestowed by the contract. Han gave Yue her own copy, which could travel in her personal notes because it described her employment. Official household records stayed with their keepers. The writing board would return at initial closure and be checked out anew for the new term, keeping each term's loans distinct.

harbor_p10_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_021.text: He Ming hugged Yue outside the office and then apologized for making a public scene. Yue said the hug was acceptable and the apology unnecessary. Han arrived carrying the draft roster and pretended annoyance that practical work waited while they celebrated. The women invited her into the embrace, trapping a corner of the roster between coats. She complained until she laughed. The paper survived with a crease. They would copy its public version cleanly. Friendship had finally caused a small documentation problem everyone could admit without making it evidence that care and competence were natural enemies.

harbor_p10_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_022.text: Yan heard the news at the dry work gate. He offered congratulations and asked whether the new term included a person responsible when Yue was not present. She named the contact clerk. He said good, then asked if the kite could serve as a second messenger. Yue said its route record was unreliable. The foreman grinned and returned to his crew. His welcome stayed brief because the next ordinary load needed attention. That brevity pleased Yue. The harbor could be glad she remained without stopping its work to prove she had become the necessary center of it.

harbor_p10_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_023.text: The initial term's last paid half-day went to final source comparison and handover. Yue checked the old household inquiry references, refund completion, ongoing crew referral and property dispositions. Unknown unrelated bundles remained under commercial custody with their own notices; she did not invent closure. Han accepted the page count and source links. The administrator received the report as an account of a finite job, not a claim every promise in town now worked. Twenty-four half-days were complete. Yue felt the last date settle into the ledger with a satisfaction that made the new term feel cleaner rather than less affectionate.

harbor_p10_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_024.text: The office paid Yue the final four copper since the previous twenty-two-shift wage record, bringing earned and paid initial wages to forty-eight. She counted it and signed the receipt. The repair shed keeper submitted the agreed seventy-two for term bed and meals, which the office checked and paid through its own line. Copies ten, interpretation twelve and ferries six matched actual receipts. Total spending closed at one hundred forty-eight. Forty-four remained unspent operations authority. The initial appointment no longer had an open expense line waiting for someone to fill it because a round number looked more complete.

harbor_p10_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_025.text: Yue returned the board, numbered pencils and unused blank forms. Han inspected ordinary wear and recorded the return, charging no invented damage for a pencil honestly shortened through use. The official inquiry pages remained filed. Personal practice notes and her own contract copy stayed with Yue. The new appointment would issue the necessary loans again at its start. For one evening, her pack and shelf held no harbor equipment at all. The small interval mattered. She could still leave with bedding, cup, blade, notes and wrapped pendant without forgetting which possessions she actually owned.

harbor_p10_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_026.text: The administrator closed the original appropriation record with one hundred forty-eight spent and forty-four unspent returned to eligible operations control. The newly reserved two hundred stood separately for the next term. The office did not describe the unspent forty-four as money recovered from claimants. No claimant had supplied it. He Ming asked to see the public aggregate because she wanted to understand the job she had urged Yue to keep. Han explained each purpose. The woman said it was remarkable how an office could avoid a wrong story simply by saying who paid before listing what it bought.

harbor_p10_027.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_027.text: The term report's public summary credited staff and claimant sources. It did not put Yue's name above every useful result. She reviewed the wording and asked for the interpreter and creek keepers to be visible within appropriate privacy limits. Han agreed. The story contained a successful rescue and several completed accounts, but its title was a finite inquiry completion, not the harbor saved. He Ming approved the restraint after laughing at how absurd the grander heading would sound beside another boat still needing repair. A town could thank somebody without pretending its troubles were a stage waiting for one hero.

harbor_p10_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_028.text: Qin's trainee visited the completion meeting to explain the closed guarantee account if questions remained. Qin stayed at the gardens, having arranged her authority and ordinary duty coverage. She gave the arithmetic correctly and answered one question by opening the rule instead of guessing. Yue liked seeing the custodian absent without the process failing. Han said this was the result they wanted for contact work too. The trainee asked whether that meant Yue hoped people stopped needing her. Yue answered that she hoped they could need the task without needing one particular person to be awake and nearby.

harbor_p10_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_029.text: On the way back from the shore, Yue stopped at a small blade repair stall. Her knife had dulled from use on cords, cloth and food since the forest journey. The repairer inspected it and quoted a private price before sharpening. Yue paid from her own earnings, not an inquiry expense line. He asked whether a cultivator needed an enchanted edge. She said she needed this one to cut cleanly without slipping. He approved the answer and told her where the tang should be checked next season. Ordinary possessions lasted through ordinary care, which rarely appeared in anyone's grand account.

harbor_p10_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_030.text: The repairer's daughter wanted to know whether luminous hands left fingerprints. Yue said she had never used them to touch a wet paint wall for research. The child offered the side of their stall as a test. Her father objected before Yue could decline. They laughed, and the sharpened blade returned in its familiar wrap. Yue used no qi at the market. She bought an apple and sliced it with hands beside the stall, pleased by the improvement. A tool could become more useful without becoming a new possession or claiming a higher earned rank.

harbor_p10_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_031.text: At the net shed, Wu Lian was learning which window had to close before evening wind reached the rented room. Her sister helped carry bedding from the temporary lodging arrangement. The two children argued over the brighter corner, while the duck tested every place adults called unsuitable. Wu asked Yue, passing on a free walk, to hold a bowl while she moved a shelf. Yue held it and left when the family resumed its task. The room was neither a completed housing remedy nor a misery requiring an official witness. It was a household working out where to put things.

harbor_p10_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_032.text: Wu's sister said the two-week agreement ended soon and a longer stay would cost more. The landlord could offer a new rate, not a promise to keep the rescue price indefinitely. Wu wanted time to compare it with her canteen wages before deciding. Her sister urged returning inland, which would mean another uncertain job. They did not ask Yue to choose. She listened until Wu asked where the public housing adviser sat this week. Yue supplied the actual location. A useful friend could know one practical thing without turning another woman's private discussion into a case that belonged to her.

harbor_p10_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_033.text: Aning's father came to the market with a recovered cloth bundle and found his daughter practicing sums. He no longer asked her to leave the trial shift immediately. He asked whether she could inspect two lengths after supper. She agreed to a bounded family task. The aunt watched, pleased enough to become unbearable with advice. Aning begged her not to celebrate every question as evidence her father had learned a new way to live. He laughed and said he would certainly make mistakes enough to spoil that theory. They returned to work without needing a perfect reconciliation.

harbor_p10_034.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_034.text: Fen listened to Aning describe the exchange while they waited for the binder to unlock the paper room. She said her father now asked when she wanted to talk, then chose the exact moment she most wanted silence. Aning said this still counted as progress. Fen replied that progress should learn to knock. They laughed, young enough to enjoy correcting adults and old enough to know the jokes had cost something. Yue overheard only the laughter through the open door. The girls sounded less lonely than when the harbor received them. Yue needed no report to be glad.

harbor_p10_035.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_035.text: Dai Min refused a customer who wanted a large net repaired at a smaller net's price. He said her late husband always accepted the rate. She asked for the old order record if he relied on it. He produced none and complained she had become difficult. Dai felt shaken after he left, then relieved she kept the work from becoming an obligation she could not afford. He Ming stayed with her while she calculated the hours honestly. They found another buyer later. Yue heard privately how recovered wages made refusing one unfair job possible while future trade remained difficult.

harbor_p10_036.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_036.text: Peng Li repaired Wen's second shelf under a price they argued about in advance. He used his own recovered adze and the lender's plane only after arranging another agreed loan. The lender mocked the written return date, then insisted it be legible. Peng said nobody in the harbor could enjoy a joke without turning it into stationery anymore. Wen said the shelf would be cheaper if they stopped talking. Their irritation made the work feel almost festive. Yue visited that afternoon and offered no inspection opinion beyond noticing the shelf stood level. Enough people already cared about his screws.

harbor_p10_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_037.text: Qin's trainee brought him a difficult late-claim question after the closed guarantee review. He asked her to identify which rule applied before recalling an old case. She did, then found the source differed from the case he remembered. He thanked her for the difference. Later, he told Yue at the gardens that memory was useful until it tried to become authority by itself. She understood why he liked training more than he expected. Another keeper could protect his work from familiar confidence. He returned to onions without needing to be the only keeper who knew the ledger.

harbor_p10_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_038.text: The gardener insisted Qin stop moving seedlings when leaves bent. The custodian said he merely checked conditions. The gardener said plants had no appeal route against overattention. He Ming, arriving for a pot, delighted in that verdict. Qin told her she was no better with her room plant. She conceded the charge and paid the price. Their exchange gave Yue an idea for an evening with no harbor work: cook whatever the garden could spare and let nobody write a conclusion. The plan failed at once because the boy demanded minutes from the fish kite's council. They refused him collectively.

harbor_p10_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_039.text: Sui Yan spent a free morning baking the recipe her son sent. This time she followed the step she skipped before. The loaf rose better and scorched at the base. She took the sound slices to the duty room and ate the damaged ones herself until an assistant told her this was foolish accounting. She laughed and shared those too after trimming the worst edge. Yue heard the story at supper. The captain's life could contain a failure that harmed nobody beyond a disappointing mouthful. People responsible for dangerous tasks still needed places where mistakes could remain small.

harbor_p10_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_040.text: Yan Su went fishing with Deren from a licensed dry bank on their free afternoon. Neither man caught anything. Deren said the fish could sense pending liability findings and refused association. Yan said they could sense cheap bait. They argued until Bo arrived carrying better bait bought with his own money. The young rigger caught the first fish, making the afternoon intolerable to both elders. Yue met them returning and admired the catch without asking whether the meeting proved friendship had healed every question. It proved they could spend a free day together while an independent reviewer still owed answers.

harbor_p10_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_041.text: Deren gave the fish to Dai Min because she had repaired his coat while he recovered and declined payment for that particular gift. He asked whether she wanted it before arriving with a dripping bundle. She did. At supper, she said the fish was too small for the amount of dignity the men lost acquiring it. He Ming repeated the joke to Yan, who threatened to charge an entertainment fee. Nobody paid it. The private chain of gifts stayed outside public compensation accounts. Clear gifts and agreed work made generosity less anxious.

harbor_p10_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_042.text: The platform reviewer sent a status explaining why final findings required another maintenance source. Deren read it with irritation and a clearer idea of the gap. Immediate treatment support remained recorded; his lost-work question had a review date. Yue's initial report included that limit only where it mattered to the harbor contact route. She could not close the injury claim by declaring the rescue successful or calling Yan a friend. Deren said he appreciated a notice that gave him something concrete to challenge. He would challenge the late search through the review desk, rather than make Yue a tribunal.

harbor_p10_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_043.text: The shore navigation review after the barge grounding found the removed stake absent from the chart update. The competent keeper identified an earlier survey gap and directed a marked inspection before further traffic used that line. Responsibility and any loss claim still needed separate sources. The barge pilot supplied his course record and received the findings within his access rights. Yue did not witness the survey but read the public status. The episode gave the contact proposal another example: a person should learn what was found without being told that one useful correction settled every disputed cost linked to it.

harbor_p10_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_044.text: Shui Rong arranged a new crew contact point before taking shore inventory work at another berth. She delivered the change herself to the assigned adviser, preserving the contract reference. He Ming offered to carry a private family message separately and was accepted. The worker said she disliked depending on clerks but could see why a stable point mattered when jobs moved people daily. The women bought tea after the visit. Yue joined them on her free walk and heard Shui describe a childhood village with no quay. Her love of boats existed before this wage question and would survive it.

harbor_p10_045.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_045.text: Luo Tai sent his parent the undisputed wages he actually received through an ordinary remittance route. He kept the receipt and waited for the grounding-time decision. He had feared disputing anything would cost the whole payment. The adviser separated the questions clearly enough for him to act. He still wanted another voyage and would weigh its contract against the current risk. Yue declined to call that choice foolish. Work offered people different kinds of insecurity. The point was to preserve information and a usable question, rather than make everyone prove courage by choosing the road she would have preferred.

harbor_p10_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_046.text: The office received a thank-you note from Qiao Bensheng's nephew with the old man's complaint written underneath. The blanket with the red patch had been correct; the shoes remained unforgivable. Han read the permitted public feedback aloud and laughed. The shelter's receiving process had worked for that passenger without controlling the family's next arrangement. He Ming wanted the report to include that kind of success as well as wage numbers. Han agreed, naming the task and source while keeping private household details closed. A living result could be visible without requiring the whole family to display gratitude for an audience.

harbor_p10_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_047.text: Wu Lian's children visited the repair shed with their mother to show the duck's egg. The boy declared it evidence of productive refugee employment. Wu said the duck was no refugee in a legal sense and had no wage contract. Fen told them all to leave the egg out of the harbor's finances. They boiled it through kitchen permission and divided it into tiny pieces everyone mostly tasted laughter. Yue contributed bread privately. The scene used nothing from the rescue stores or inquiry meal account. A household that arrived frightened could offer something freely without being charged for the favor.

harbor_p10_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_048.text: Han asked Fen to review a draft instruction for people sending safe-contact requests. The binder approved a paid shop task through the office's regular copying budget, separate from Yue's closed or closing expense line. Fen spotted a sentence that made silence sound like refusal. Han revised it to distinguish no reply from a declined request. The girl felt proud and uncomfortable because the distinction belonged to her own weeks waiting for Luo. Han thanked her for the specific reading. Fen said she preferred earning for useful criticism rather than being praised for having suffered enough to understand a bad sentence.

harbor_p10_049.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_049.text: The administrator asked whether the new contact term could start by improving every current form. Yue answered that twenty-eight half-days could not carry all revisions and live outreach without priorities. Han proposed testing a set first. Sui wanted urgent handling boundaries clear; He Ming wanted people who could not attend to receive replies. The meeting named the first fortnight's tasks and responsible staff. No permanent service was promised. The contract's two hundred copper and fourteen weeks were real precisely because they had limits. Yue signed the final schedule with less anxiety than she had felt facing the draft's attractive list.

harbor_p10_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_050.text: The repair shed keeper reserved Yue's room through the new term at the agreed eighty-four bed-and-meal total, payable by the office under invoices. The new agreement did not reimburse her first private nights from arrival or the Reed Steps lodging she chose to pay herself. Those costs remained historical personal expenses. The keeper inspected her room bedding and renewed its use. Yue's own bedding stayed in her pack. The woman asked whether she wanted another shelf for papers. Yue declined because official papers would stay at the office, and personal notes already had a place she could carry.

harbor_p10_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_051.text: Yue wrote the forest commission a personal letter saying her first harbor term closed and she chose another bounded appointment. She paid postage herself. She described no protected family record and claimed no cultivation advance. The wording felt plain enough to disappoint an imagined reader wanting adventure. Then she remembered the trapped worker, Fen's shore journey, and the barge rescue she did not personally perform. Adventure had occurred. She did not need to borrow everyone else's danger to make her own letter interesting. She wrote that friends made the town harder to leave and sealed the page before adding more.

harbor_p10_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_052.text: That evening, Han asked what Yue put in the letter. She shared the part about friends and withheld nothing private because none had entered it. The clerk looked pleased, then embarrassed. He Ming said friendship was a defensible reason for staying if the wages also worked. Yan said the room mattered too; he would never trust a commission that ignored where a person slept. Sui said bread mattered most and passed her scorched loaf. Their mock argument left Yue feeling understood without being explained. The new term had a job, and the town had room for motives outside contracts.

harbor_p10_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_053.text: Before the final supper, Yue sharpened a pencil that would return to the office and checked her personal blade wrap separately. The distinction had become a habit rather than a speech. She had enough earned money for travel if the new term failed within its lawful ending provisions. She wanted that freedom recorded in her mind, not displayed as distrust of friends. The pack's familiar weight reassured her. Staying did not require becoming a person unable to leave. She set it beneath the bed and went downstairs, where the boy had started another absurd argument about the kite's future cabinet.

harbor_p10_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_054.text: He Ming bought extra rice for the closing supper after checking what each guest planned to bring. She refused her brother's offer of a fish if it meant arriving with something nobody could cook in time. He Jun accused her of destroying spontaneous generosity. She said spontaneity could buy onions instead. He did, and the meal improved. Yue enjoyed watching a woman once burdened by other people's uncertain promises negotiate something as ordinary as dinner. The humor came from a real change: He Ming could ask what an offer meant before accepting responsibility for whatever followed it through her door.

harbor_p10_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_055.text: Han reached the supper early enough to help set the table. She put the roster draft safely inside her own office bag and left it closed all evening. He Ming noticed and made no joke. The clerk had spent months being the person everyone could approach with a paper. Tonight she could be approached with a dish. Yue handed her cups and accepted the place set beside the window. Neither woman needed to earn friendship by making another useful announcement before the meal. Outside, the harbor bell marked a duty change assigned to people who had not come to supper.

harbor_p10_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_056.text: Sui arrived after a properly arranged handover, her duty keeper named on the roster. Yan came after his crew's load work ended. Their presence at supper depended on responsible coverage, but they did not recite it at the table. Deren brought the successful fish joke for one more telling and protested the absence of his royalty payment. Fen charged him a laugh and declared the account balanced. Dai Min smiled at the tablecloth she gave. Yue watched the room fill, knowing the new term would bring unforeseen disappointments. She remained glad without expecting the new term to stay easy.

harbor_p10_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_057.text: The last evening of the twelfth week brought supper at He Ming's room. Everyone paid or contributed through clear private agreement rather than charge the inquiry. He Jun cooked the fish badly enough that his sister took over its sauce. Han brought peas, Yan bread, Sui the sharp onion relish she finally learned to eat in smaller portions. Fen came after work with her father. The room was crowded and cheerful. Yue's first harbor term had ended. The next would begin tomorrow, but tonight nobody asked her to turn supper into proof its two hundred copper would succeed.

harbor_p10_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_058.text: Dai Min arrived late carrying a repaired cloth as a gift she chose. He Ming asked whether she wanted payment because sewing was her work. Dai said the cloth was for the table, not a hidden order, and she wanted to give it. The woman accepted without performing an argument about generosity. Yue watched the exchange and thought they had all become more willing to ask what an act meant. The new habit could be tiring. Tonight it made room for a freely given object whose value did not need to become an obligation assigned to the recipient.

harbor_p10_059.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_059.text: The boy appeared with the fish kite and demanded a place at supper for its gull passenger. He Ming told him the kite could hang where it would not touch food. Yan inspected the hook and declared it suitable for imaginary cargo. Fen said he lacked jurisdiction over fictional seas. Sui offered to quarantine the argument if it became noisy. Everyone laughed, including Luo, who knew the jokes through his daughter. Yue felt the harbor turning into a place she might miss. That feeling belonged to her life, not to the job whose new start date waited in the office.

harbor_p10_060.speaker: narrator
harbor_p10_060.text: After supper, Yue walked home with Han under stars the harbor lamps made difficult to see. The clerk asked whether she regretted staying already. Yue said no and might sometimes regret it later, because decisions were allowed ordinary bad days. Han liked that answer. She said painting would probably produce another one tomorrow. They passed the office shutters without stopping to inspect notices. The two terms had a clean boundary. Work would reopen in the morning. Tonight their friendship could take the road past the desk without checking whether another question had been left beneath it.
